input.brief: gitseed: git hosting over BitTorrent DHT that cannot be taken down or silently replaced once one other person has a copy

direction.name: Dressed as something else
direction.idea: Art-direct the subject as if it belonged to a different, more vivid category. A money app is sold like a streetwear drop. An industrial roaster is presented like a design object. Drilling hardware gets the calm of a watch brand. A parcel-locker service becomes a fairground of stickers. Choose the borrowed category by asking what feeling the audience is missing from this kind of product (swagger, calm, glamour, play) and which category owns that feeling. Then take its manners completely: its type, its pacing, its way of photographing things. The contrast between dull subject and vivid dress is what people remember.
direction.composition: Depends on the borrowed category, so decide it explicitly and write it in your notes. Fashion drop: one shouted condensed headline across the full width, a single cropped image under it, then product facts as a blunt list. Watch or perfume: a centred object on a dark field, a small serif name, very few words, long vertical pauses. Poster or zine: flat colour blocks, heavy type, tilted cut-out images. Museum: one item per screen on a plinth-like band of colour with a short label beside it. Whichever you choose, the page structure stays simple (four to six sections) and every section uses the borrowed manners, including pricing and the footer.
direction.typography: The borrowed category's type, fully committed: condensed and loud, or refined and small. No halfway.
direction.colour: The borrowed category's palette, which will be unlike the subject's sector norm. That mismatch is intended.
direction.imagery: Photograph the subject the way the borrowed category would be photographed. With the dealt set, choose images for attitude, not literal relevance, and crop them hard.
direction.richness: Attitude. The page has a recognisable voice from another world, applied to a subject nobody expected it for.
direction.pitfalls: Name the borrowed category in one word before you start, or the result is merely loud. The content must still be clear: what it is, what it costs, how to get it. Avoid borrowing from 'tech startup', which is the default you are escaping.

hero.name: Flush-left shout, seam photograph
hero.blueprint: Borrowed from a street poster or zine. A saturated flat field covers the top 82% of the viewport; a second flat colour forms a band across the bottom 18%. The headline is two lines in an ultra-heavy face at clamp(80px, 12vw, 190px), flush left on a 20px margin, leading 0.84, reaching about 62% across the width; its first line starts 16% below the top. Right of centre one photograph is stuck on like a poster scrap: a 3:4 portrait 30% of the viewport wide (columns 8-11), clipped to an arch with clip-path or a large top border-radius, rotated 5 degrees, its top edge leaving the viewport and its lower edge straddling the seam so it sits on both colours. The photograph overlaps the last letters of the first line by about 4vw and lies above the type in the stacking order. On the bottom band, on one baseline: one supporting sentence at 20px on the left (max 40ch) and the single action, a chunky rectangle in the upper field's colour, at the right. The wordmark sits top-left at 20px; three text links top-right.
hero.mobile: The field takes the top 78% and the band the rest. The headline sets at 19vw on two lines flush to 16px margins, starting at 12% of the height. The arch photograph moves under the type: 58% of the width, pushed against the right edge and cropped by it, still tilted 5 degrees and straddling the seam. The sentence and the full-width action stack on the band.
hero.headline: A 2-4 word shout, at most 16 characters, lowercase or capitals throughout, one or two words per line.

type.note: A true didone with hairline serifs and vertical stress over a light geometric sans, the classic fashion-magazine pairing. Suits luxury property, jewellery, fragrance and fashion.

palette.name: Grey, mint, orange
palette.note: Black on white to start, then whole sections flood with flat mid-grey, acid mint and orange in turn. Photographs inside a flooded section are shown in black-and-white, and mint is also the button colour on white and black.

photos.title: Fog and quiet
photos.note: misty, muted, minimal landscapes and empty horizons; calm areas for text

photos.alt: Road lined with tall trees fading into thick fog
Layered hill ridges fading into warm beige mist
Silky long-exposure sea beneath a blue and orange sunset sky

motion.name: Shutter image
motion.description: The one hero or showcase image opens from an edge with a clip-path over about 1.1 seconds while the picture inside settles from 1.12 scale to rest. Use it once, on the image that matters most; later images simply are there. Recipe: 'Image shutter' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Lit panel, dark row
sections.blueprint: One dark field, 96svh tall. Across its middle runs a horizontal row of five to seven interface panels, each a different true-size fragment marked data-ui (an open menu, an inspector, a composer, a chart card), 320–460px wide at their natural heights, vertically centred and 26vw apart. The row scrolls sideways with scroll-snap-type: x mandatory and scroll-snap-align: center, and can be dragged. Only the panel at the centre is lit: full opacity, in the product's light theme, the brightest thing on screen. The others sit at 22% opacity and are inert. The viewport's edges crop the outermost panels. In the gap to the right of the centred panel, top-aligned with it, a 24ch column gives its name at 24px in a light weight and two lines at 16px in a lifted ink; this text changes as panels arrive. There is no heading above the row.
sections.mobile: The row is 62svh tall; panels snap one per screen at true size, capped at 86vw wide, with neighbours showing 7vw at each side at 22% opacity. The name and its two lines sit beneath the row on the left margin and change with the centred panel. Swiping moves the row.

sections.name: Many into one
sections.blueprint: A diagram drawn with one repeated shape instead of arrows. The heading (two to four words on two lines at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px)) and a short paragraph at 17px sit in columns 1–4. Beneath, a wide inline SVG spans columns 1–12 at about 4.5:1. It is built from 120–160 small filled squares (or the page's own motif), each 10–14px. In the left third they are scattered loosely in two pale tones. In the middle third they are pulled into a tight horizontal ribbon three squares high. In the right third they fan out again into neat, evenly spaced rows in the accent colour. The eye reads disorder, compression, order, from left to right. Under the diagram, three text columns aligned to its thirds: a bold one-word name at 20px and two lines at 16px each; the words carry the sequence ('Gather', 'Reduce', 'Release'). No connecting marks.
sections.mobile: The diagram turns to run top to bottom: a 3:4 SVG with the scatter at the top, the ribbon as a vertical band in the middle and the ordered rows at the bottom. The three names and their text sit to its right in a 38vw column, each level with its zone.

sections.name: Specimens on colour tiles
sections.blueprint: Each capability is represented by one object photographed alone and shown on a flat colour tile. Columns 1–3 hold the heading (two to four words at 40–52px), top-aligned, with a 30ch sentence beneath and nothing else down the rest of that column. Columns 4–12 hold a grid of five or six tiles in two rows with 10px gaps: tiles are 4:5 except one, which is double width at 8:5 and placed second in the first row. Tile colours rotate through three palette fields. Each photograph is centred at about 70% of its tile's height; on light tiles use mix-blend-mode: multiply so a white studio background disappears. Under each tile, outside it and aligned to its left edge: the capability name at 20px medium and one fact at 16px in the soft ink. No text on the tiles and no hover lift.
sections.mobile: The heading and its sentence sit on top at full width. Tiles become a two-column grid with 8px gaps; the double tile spans both columns at 8:5 and comes first. Names shrink to 17px and facts to 15px, still under each tile.

sections.name: Recognition as a table
sections.blueprint: Awards, press mentions or credits set as a four-column table with no lines. The heading is two or three words at about 5vw, stepped over two lines with the second line indented by two columns, and occupies columns 1–7. The table begins 72px below and spans columns 1–12 on a fixed grid: year in columns 1–2, project or title in 3–6, awarding body or publication in 7–10, the award itself in 11–12, right-aligned. Rows are set at 16–17px with 14px of padding above and below; every second row carries a background tone one step from the ground, running the full table width, which replaces rules. Year groups are separated by one blank row, and the year is printed only on the first row of its group. Use a real `<table>` with `border-collapse: collapse` and no borders.
sections.mobile: The heading drops to 11vw. Each table row becomes a two-line block: title on the first line in the full ink, then body and award on the second in the softer ink. The year stands once as a 22px figure above its group. Alternate blocks keep the background tone.

sections.name: Tabbed index cards
sections.blueprint: Questions are filed like cards in a drawer. A heading of two to four words at about 4vw sits in columns 3–10. Beneath it, in the same columns, five or six filled panels are stacked so that each overlaps the one above, leaving 96px of every card showing. Each card has a tab on its top edge, 200px wide and 40px tall, stepping right by 150px per card, cut with `clip-path: polygon()` so card and tab are one filled shape. The cards rotate through two or three palette colours. The tab carries the topic in one or two words at 16px; the visible strip under it shows the question at 20px medium. Choosing a card expands it to show the answer at 17px over at most 50ch and pushes the cards below it down. One card is open at a time; the first is open on load.
sections.mobile: Cards run full width with the same overlap, 88px of each showing. Tabs shrink to 120px wide and step right by 48px per card. The open card expands in place with its answer at 16px and 20px padding, and the heading leads at 9vw.

sections.name: The printed menu sheet
sections.blueprint: The list is one tall sheet of paper. A filled paper-colour panel 640px wide sits centred, or offset to columns 7–12, on a contrasting flat ground or a full-bleed photograph, with square corners and its top and bottom edges cut into shallow scallops by `clip-path` or an SVG `mask`. Inside, 64px padding and a centred, symmetrical setting like a printed card: the venue or section name at 40–48px, a one-line note at 15px, then three or four groups 56px apart. Each group opens with its name at 22px, centred. Items follow at 17px with 16px between them: the dish or service at the left of a 420px measure, the price at the right with tabular figures, and a one-line description at 14px in the soft ink under the name. Alignment alone links name and price; there are no leaders. The sheet ends with the opening hours as two centred lines. Holds 12–24 items.
sections.mobile: The sheet spans the screen with 10px of ground showing at each side and 28px padding; the scalloped edges stay at top and bottom. The measure is the full inner width and prices stay right-aligned. Group names at 20px, items at 16px.

sections.name: One word is the button
sections.blueprint: The entire band is one link. A full-bleed field in the accent colour, about 60svh tall, contains a single verb of four to eight letters set at 24–30vw in the heaviest weight, tight tracking, sized with `clamp()` so it spans the content width on one line with its baseline 24px above the bottom edge. The `<a>` wraps the whole band; on hover and focus the field and the word swap colours instantly. In the top-left corner, at 20px, one sentence says what happens next; in the top-right, an arrow drawn as a simple inline SVG, 48px, points up and right. There is no other button anywhere in the section. In a page with a motif, the band's top corners take the motif's shape (a large radius, or a chamfer cut with `clip-path`). Keep the word honest: the action itself, not a slogan.
sections.mobile: The band is 46svh tall. The word is set at whatever size fills the width on one line; choose a shorter verb rather than going below 22vw. Sentence top-left at 17px across two lines, arrow top-right at 32px. The whole band stays tappable.

sections.name: Invitation over a cropped name
sections.blueprint: Close and footer in one full-viewport field of the inverse colour. Upper third, columns 1–7: a two-line invitation at about 5vw, three to five words, with one filled rectangular button beneath it. At columns 10–12, top-aligned with the invitation, three or four social or contact links stacked at 16px. The wordmark fills the bottom of the screen at 26–30vw on one line, `white-space: nowrap`, heavier and larger than the viewport can hold: it is pushed down with `transform: translateY(30%)` so the bottom edge cuts through the letters, and a long name also runs off the right edge. `overflow: hidden` on the footer does the cropping. One row of credits and legal links at 13px sits directly above the wordmark's cap line, spread left and right. The cropped name must be recognisable from its upper two-thirds alone; test that it is.
sections.mobile: Invitation at 11vw on two lines at the top with a full-width button. Links follow as one row of words at 15px. The wordmark sits at 34vw at the bottom, cropped by both the bottom and the right edge, with the legal row above it at 12px.

references.name: UGLYCASH
references.idea: A money app sold like streetwear: one shouted condensed headline over the phone, then sticker-covered 3D props where feature icons would normally go.
references.hero: Near-white page. A floating light-grey nav bar only 35% of the viewport wide sits centred 20px from the top: condensed wordmark left, two social icons in the middle, an app button with a glowing magenta outline right. Directly beneath, a two-line uppercase headline in bold condensed grotesque at 11.4vw, centred, leading under 0.9, about 60% of the width, with a faint cyan and magenta fringe on the letter edges; it fills the band from 12% to 43% of the height. A single phone mockup 27% of the viewport wide rises immediately under the headline, centred, cut off by the bottom edge. Its magenta screen glow is the only colour.
references.type: Helvetica Now Display Condensed Bold in capitals at 164px with -0.033em tracking and very tight leading; the same face in mixed case near 34px for section headings. Inter at 14px, semi-bold, for captions. Two faces and a roughly 12:1 jump.
references.colour: #f7f7f7 #000000 #ffffff #ff00e6 #b6ff00 #00aeef — Off-white ground, white cards, black type. Neon magenta, lime and cyan appear only as whole-card fills, glows and stickers, never in text. Cool and synthetic overall.
references.imagery: Phone mockups with real app screens, plus glossy 3D props (money bags, a holographic card, an eagle, a wet-floor sign, banknotes) covered in die-cut stickers, each centred in a rounded card; some cards have grainy neon gradients.
references.layout: Content sits in a centred column about 60% of the viewport wide. Sections open with a left-aligned condensed heading, then rows of two or three rounded cards with captions placed outside and below. A horizontal carousel and a centred uppercase statement break the rhythm.

sections.description: A left-aligned two-line condensed heading near 34px above a row of three equal cards with 8px gaps and small radius: one pale grey with a cropped balance readout and tilted stickers, one white with two 3D money bags, one solid cyan with a phone cropped at the bottom. Captions sit beneath each card rather than inside: a bold one-word title and two short 13px lines.

Two near-square cards side by side, each half the column. Left: a grainy lime-to-lilac gradient with a white floating panel listing three rows, each with a flag, a label and a small pill button. Right: a white card with a black holographic payment card tilted about 25 degrees, stickers stuck to it. A later pair repeats the pattern with a solid magenta card holding a white icon-grid panel.

Trust carousel: a horizontal row of tall cards, each showing one 3D object centred (a chrome eagle on white, a banknote on solid lime, a yellow wet-floor sign with hand-lettered warning). The title sits inside the first card and below the others. A tiny two-dot pager is centred underneath and the next card peeks in orange at the right edge of the column.

A white rounded panel the width of the column in which the wordmark is scaled to fill the panel edge to edge, about 55% of the viewport, in black ultra-condensed capitals. Beneath it, one row with a small parent-brand credit at left and two store badges at right, then legal small print in 11px at left and four right-aligned links.

steal: Make the nav a short floating bar a third of the viewport wide so the headline can start almost at the top edge.
Replace feature icons with one photoreal 3D prop per card, each covered in die-cut stickers, and keep captions outside the card.
End with the wordmark scaled to exactly fill a white footer card, with all legal text beneath it at 11px.

references.name: Vero New-York
references.idea: Treat a keepsake like couture: a slow close-up film opens, then a white 3D sculpture of a dress stays pinned at centre while one sentence in mixed capitals and italics passes over it.
references.hero: Full-bleed video with no scrim: an extreme close-up of a woman's profile against a burnt-orange wall, a blurred pale sculpture occupying the right 40% of the frame in the foreground. Exactly at centre sits the four-letter wordmark in white serif capitals, about 240px wide; 25px beneath it a one-line tagline at 20px alternates italic lowercase connectives with roman capitals. Two translucent frosted rectangles with square corners float 30px from the top corners: a 130px menu button left, a 250px commission button right, both in small capitals. A tiny chevron marks the bottom centre. Nothing else; the image carries the screen.
references.type: Louize Display at 120px (8.3vw), centred: nouns in roman capitals, connective words in lowercase italic at the same size within the same line. Beausite Classic grotesk appears only for a bold 17px lead and footer links. Serif body runs 11–16px; the footer wordmark fills the width.
references.colour: #f3f0ed #181615 #b4521f #c6a788 #ffffff #97775a — Burnt orange and skin tones in the opening film, then warm off-white pages with near-black type and a plaster-white sculpture; orange returns only inside one small photograph.
references.imagery: Shallow-focus warm video up top; a real-time 3D plaster-white bust and lace dress on off-white, cropped at neck and hem and fading into the page; one small square-cornered photo of the dress on a plinth against orange.
references.layout: Everything sits on one centre axis with wide empty flanks. Two fixed corner buttons persist as soft-shadowed white tiles. Headlines take two lines each and share the screen with the pinned 3D object; body text is confined to a 240px centred column.

sections.description: Off-white screen. The sentence is delivered in halves: first two centred lines at 8.3vw in the upper third, with a small diamond glyph beside the italic word, while a white 3D bust rises from the bottom centre at about 30% of the width. Scrolling turns the sculpture to show the laced back, now filling the full height of the centre column, and the second half of the sentence lands over the skirt in the lower third.

The skirt's hem dissolves into the off-white at the top of the screen. Beneath it is a centred text stack only about 240px wide: a three-line lead in bold grotesk at 17px, four lines of serif body at 11px, and a small white rectangular button with a diffuse shadow carrying the same italic-plus-capitals label as the header button. The lower half of the viewport is left empty.

A tiny centred eyebrow in the italic-plus-capitals style, then a two-line headline at about 8vw where each line begins with a lowercase italic word and ends in capitals, the lines offset so the block reads as a stagger. Under it, centred, one small photo about 330×290px with square corners: saturated orange backdrop, white dress on a plinth. The image is deliberately much smaller than the type.

Off-white. Top-left, a five-item vertical link list in small grotesk; under it a newsletter field drawn as a single underline with an arrow; three social links right-aligned at the same level. Then the wordmark in near-black serif capitals stretches across the full width, about 45% of the viewport tall. A final row of tiny grey legal links sits beneath.

steal: Within one serif headline, set the nouns in roman capitals and the small connective words in lowercase italic at the same size.
Pin a single white 3D object on an off-white page and deliver one sentence in two halves over its front and back as it turns.
Follow a huge two-line headline with one deliberately small, saturated photograph centred beneath it instead of a full-width image.

references.name: Made With Gsap
references.idea: The hero is the product: a draggable vertical reel of effect demos runs through the middle of the headline, which is split and pushed to both edges to make room.
references.hero: White viewport. A one-line headline at 3.3vw is broken in two: the first half flush to the left margin, the second flush to the right, both on the vertical centre line. Between them a black rounded video card, 35% of the width and 16:9, sits dead centre with a mono catalogue number under its left corner; the cards before and after it peek in from the top and bottom edges. Wordmark top-left; top-right a grey capsule of mono uppercase links with a count chip, a round account button and a lime capsule button. Bottom-left a two-line 18px statement; bottom-right a grey mono drag hint.
references.type: LayGrotesk medium, tracking −0.02em, sentence case, for headlines (47px in the hero, about 5.5vw mid-page, 17vw in the closing banner) and 22px body; PP Neue Montreal Mono uppercase at 12px for nav, buttons and labels. Statements emphasise by grey-versus-white words.
references.colour: #ffffff #0a0a0b #c9fe6e #f1f1f1 #8a8a8a #1f6bff — White hero and footer bracket a long near-black middle; acid lime is reserved for join buttons and a tiny arrow, with one blue button inside the product UI. Demo thumbnails add saturated orange and teal.
references.imagery: Looping recordings of the effects: black 16:9 cards with 4px corners holding clusters of small saturated photo tiles (portraits on orange, water, flowers, architecture). Product UI appears inside a large white rounded panel.
references.layout: 24px margins, with text pinned to edges and centre rather than a column grid. White hero, then black full-viewport screens each holding one idea (statement, UI panel, logo strip, big number line), then a white rounded sheet rising over black as the footer.

sections.description: Black section. A mono eyebrow with a bullet dot is centred at the top; under it a three-line centred statement at about 2.6vw where most words are mid-grey and three key phrases are white. A two-line grey caption at 14px follows. Below, a white panel with 16px radius, 80% of the width, slides up from the bottom and contains a dark app window: effect preview at left, a methods list sidebar at right.

A row of seven overlapping circular avatars is centred, with a two-line mono uppercase caption beneath, then 60px lower a single line of white client logos runs edge to edge and is cropped at both sides as a marquee. Nothing else shares the black screen; the block sits in the lower half with a large empty area above it.

A full black viewport with one two-line statement centred at roughly 5.5vw, medium weight, tight leading: the count of effects, then the release cadence. Letters arrive individually, so mid-scroll the words are missing characters. A small dark capsule in the bottom-right corner shows which demo number is on screen, with a lime dot.

A white sheet with rounded top corners, inset 4px in the black page. The closing line is set at 17vw, centred, so large its first row is cut by the top edge; two capsule buttons (lime primary, grey secondary) sit centred beneath. The footer proper is one row: a newsletter heading and capsule input with inline submit on the left 40%, three small mono link columns on the right, and a legal line at the very bottom.

steal: Split a single-line headline in two and pin the halves to the left and right edges so the media sits inside the sentence.
Make the hero media a reel whose previous and next items peek from the top and bottom edges, signalling drag without arrows.
End on a white rounded sheet rising over a black page, with the final call set so large it is cropped by the sheet's top edge.
